cases.sentence: В четыре часа, чувствуя свое бьющееся сердце, Левин слез с извозчика у ___ и пошел дорожкой к горам и катку, наверное зная, что найдет ее там, потому что видел карету Щербацких у подъезда.
cases.explain: «Зоологического сада» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: At four o’clock, conscious of his throbbing heart, Levin stepped out of a hired sledge at the Zoological Gardens, and turned along the path to the frozen mounds and the skating ground, knowing that he would certainly find her there, as he had seen the Shtcherbatskys’ carriage at the entrance.

cases.sentence: Все катавшиеся, казалось, совершенно равнодушно обгоняли, догоняли ее, даже говорили с ней и совершенно независимо от нее веселились, пользуясь ___ и хорошею погодой.
cases.explain: «отличным льдом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: On that day of the week and at that time of day people of one set, all acquainted with one another, used to meet on the ice. There were crack skaters there, showing off their skill, and learners clinging to chairs with timid, awkward movements, boys, and elderly people skating with hygienic motives. They seemed to Levin an elect band of blissful beings because they were here, near her. All the skaters, it seemed, with perfect self-possession, skated towards her, skated by her, even spoke to her, and were happy, quite apart from her, enjoying the capital ice and the fine weather.

cases.sentence: Николай Щербацкий, ___ Кити, в коротенькой жакетке и узких панталонах, сидел с коньками на ногах на скамейке и, увидав Левина, закричал ему:
cases.explain: «двоюродный брат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Nikolay Shtcherbatsky, Kitty’s cousin, in a short jacket and tight trousers, was sitting on a garden seat with his skates on. Seeing Levin, he shouted to him:

cases.sentence: – А, первый ___!
cases.explain: «русский конькобежец» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah, the first skater in Russia! Been here long? First-rate ice—do put your skates on.”

cases.sentence: Она была на угле и, тупо поставив ___ в вы ботинках, видимо робея, катилась к нему, Отчаянно махавший руками и пригибавшийся к земле мальчик в русском платье обгонял ее.
cases.explain: «узкие ножки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I haven’t got my skates,” Levin answered, marveling at this boldness and ease in her presence, and not for one second losing sight of her, though he did not look at her. He felt as though the sun were coming near him. She was in a corner, and turning out her slender feet in their high boots with obvious timidity, she skated towards him. A boy in Russian dress, desperately waving his arms and bowed down to the ground, overtook her. She skated a little uncertainly; taking her hands out of the little muff that hung on a cord, she held them ready for emergency, and looking towards Levin, whom she had recognized, she smiled at him, and at her own fears. When she had got round the turn, she gave herself a push off with one foot, and skated straight up to Shtcherbatsky. Clutching at his arm, she nodded smiling to Levin. She was more splendid than he had imagined her.

cases.sentence: Когда он думал о ней, он мог себе живо представить ее всю, в особенности прелесть этой, с выражением детской ясности и доброты, небольшой ___, так свободно поставленной на статных девичьих плечах.
cases.explain: «белокурой головки» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: When he thought of her, he could call up a vivid picture of her to himself, especially the charm of that little fair head, so freely set on the shapely girlish shoulders, and so full of childish brightness and good humor. The childishness of her expression, together with the delicate beauty of her figure, made up her special charm, and that he fully realized. But what always struck him in her as something unlooked for, was the expression of her eyes, soft, serene, and truthful, and above all, her smile, which always transported Levin to an enchanted world, where he felt himself softened and tender, as he remembered himself in some days of his early childhood.

cases.sentence: Господи, помоги мне!» – подумал Левин и побежал к ___ с седыми букольками, сидевшей на скамейке.
cases.explain: «старой француженке» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “What’s wrong? I have offended her. Lord help me!” thought Levin, and he flew towards the old Frenchwoman with the gray ringlets, who was sitting on a bench. Smiling and showing her false teeth, she greeted him as an old friend.

cases.sentence: Поговорив о своей ___, о ее странностях, она спросила его о его жизни.
cases.explain: «старой гувернантке» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: When Levin darted up to Kitty her face was no longer stern; her eyes looked at him with the same sincerity and friendliness, but Levin fancied that in her friendliness there was a certain note of deliberate composure. And he felt depressed. After talking a little of her old governess and her peculiarities, she questioned him about his life.

cases.sentence: – Нет, не скучно, я очень занят, – сказал он, чувствуя, что она подчиняет его своему ___, из которого он не в силах будет выйти, так же, как это было в начале зимы.
cases.explain: «спокойному тону» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “No, I’m not dull, I am very busy,” he said, feeling that she was holding him in check by her composed tone, which he would not have the force to break through, just as it had been at the beginning of the winter.

cases.sentence: Мысль о том, что если он поддастся этому ее тону ___, то он опять уедет, ничего не решив, пришла ему, и он решился возмутиться.
cases.explain: «спокойной дружбы» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I don’t know,” he answered, not thinking of what he was saying. The thought that if he were held in check by her tone of quiet friendliness he would end by going back again without deciding anything came into his mind, and he resolved to make a struggle against it.

cases.sentence: Господи боже мой! помоги мне, научи меня», – говорил Левин, молясь и вместе с тем чувствуя потребность ___, разбегаясь и выписывая внешние и внутренние круги.
cases.explain: «сильного движения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “My God! what have I done! Merciful God! help me, guide me,” said Levin, praying inwardly, and at the same time, feeling a need of violent exercise, he skated about describing inner and outer circles.

cases.sentence: В это время один из ___, лучший из новых конькобежцев, с папироской во рту, в коньках, вышел из кофейной и, разбежавшись, пустился на коньках вниз по ступеням, громыхая и подпрыгивая.
cases.explain: «молодых людей» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: At that moment one of the young men, the best of the skaters of the day, came out of the coffeehouse in his skates, with a cigarette in his mouth. Taking a run, he dashed down the steps in his skates, crashing and bounding up and down. He flew down, and without even changing the position of his hands, skated away over the ice.

cases.sentence: В это время один из молодых людей, лучший из ___, с папироской во рту, в коньках, вышел из кофейной и, разбежавшись, пустился на коньках вниз по ступеням, громыхая и подпрыгивая.

cases.sentence: – Ах, это ___! – сказал Левин и тотчас же побежал наверх, чтобы сделать эту новую штуку.
cases.explain: «новая штука» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah, that’s a new trick!” said Levin, and he promptly ran up to the top to do this new trick.

cases.sentence: Левин вошел на приступки, разбежался сверху сколько мог и пустился вниз, удерживая в ___ равновесие руками.
cases.explain: «непривычном движении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Levin went to the steps, took a run from above as best he could, and dashed down, preserving his balance in this unwonted movement with his hands. On the last step he stumbled, but barely touching the ice with his hand, with a violent effort recovered himself, and skated off, laughing.

cases.sentence: «Славный, милый», – подумала Кити в это время, выходя из домика с m-lle Linon и глядя на него с улыбкой ___, как на любимого брата.
cases.explain: «тихой ласки» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “How splendid, how nice he is!” Kitty was thinking at that time, as she came out of the pavilion with Mlle. Linon, and looked towards him with a smile of quiet affection, as though he were a favorite brother. “And can it be my fault, can I have done anything wrong? They talk of flirtation. I know it’s not he that I love; but still I am happy with him, and he’s so jolly. Only, why did he say that? …” she mused.

cases.sentence: Увидав уходившую Кити и мать, встречавшую ее на ступеньках, Левин, раскрасневшийся после ___, остановился и задумался.
cases.explain: «быстрого движения» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Catching sight of Kitty going away, and her mother meeting her at the steps, Levin, flushed from his rapid exercise, stood still and pondered a minute. He took off his skates, and overtook the mother and daughter at the entrance of the gardens.

cases.sentence: – Ну что ж, едем? – спросил он. – Я все о тебе думал, и я очень рад, что ты приехал, – сказал он, с ___ глядя ему в глаза.
cases.explain: «значительным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Well, shall we set off?” he asked. “I’ve been thinking about you all this time, and I’m very, very glad you’ve come,” he said, looking him in the face with a significant air.
